newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to set up committee for first stock market.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to set up committee for first stock market.

text.p: Vietnam will set up a state stock exchange committee to speed up establishment of the fast- developing country's first bourse, official media reports said on Saturday.

The committee, which will replace an ad-hoc board set up in June last year, will comprise deputy ministers of finance, justice, planning and investment and the central bank and will prepare a legal framework for trading in stocks.
The daily Vietnam News said the committee would be accountable for granting and revoking licences to stock market players and would have overriding supervisory power.
The committee will be based in Hanoi and will have a representative office in Ho Chi Minh City, the country's commercial hub.
The Communist government, encouraged by the success of reforms along market lines, has been planning a bourse for several years.
Two foreign currency exchange centres, an embryonic form of the future stock market, were set up in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City in 1992 with limited membership.
Vietnam News said transactions at the centres, arranged on a weekly basis, amounted to little more than $1.0 million a year.
Officials acknowledge that it will be much nearer the end of the century before a flourishing stock exchange can be put in place.
So far, just 10 of the country's roughly 6,000 state-owned enterprises have been "equitised", Vietnam's term for the sale of minority stakes in companies in lieu of full privatisation.
Other obstacles in the way of a stock market include primitive accounting and a still-nascent modern banking industry.
